About The Role

This role sits within the Global Acceptance team under the Global Payments Network. Our mission is to ensure the Discover network is reliably and consistently accepted across key international markets. Within this group, the Sales Planning and Strategy team unlocks high-priority growth opportunities, partnering closely with Business Development to build market-winning plans and maximise acceptance worldwide.

The Senior Business Analyst will deliver critical strategic and analytical support to their assigned international markets. They will build territory designs, establish key performance metrics, set annual and quarterly sales targets, and deliver actionable insights that optimise sales performance. Functioning as a key thought-partner across Business Development, Product, Data Operations, and Risk, they will play a foundational role in building a rigorous, data-driven sales strategy from the ground up.

What You’ll Do

Drive Strategic Growth Plans: Lead the identification, assessment, and execution of strategic growth opportunities across your assigned markets.
Enable High-Performance Sales: Establish territory designs, sales plans, and analytical feedback loops that continuously optimize field performance.
Define Sales Goals & Targets: Set annual and quarterly sales goals for markets overall, establishing measurement frameworks that align directly with regional and global objectives.
Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate with Business Development, Product, Operations, and executive leadership to align and execute on growth priorities.
Inform Infrastructure & Tools: Serve as a key stakeholder and advisor in building best-in-class data systems, operational workflows, and sales tools.

The Skills And Experience You Need

A passion for solving analytical challenges, with a proven track record of decision-making and problem-solving based on analytics.
A STEM or Economics degree or equivalent.
Experience working in the payments industry
Impeccable written and oral communication credentials, coupled with strategic influencing skills and the ability to drive agreement.
A clear results orientation with an intense focus on achieving short and long-term goals in an uncertain and fluid environment.
Working knowledge of statistical model building, SQL querying, market research, or consulting.

Where And How You'll Work

This is a permanent position based in our London office.

We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.

What’s In It For You

We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.

Wealth & Future: Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
Holidays: Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
Health: Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
Family Support: We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.

A full list of our benefits is available here.

We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.

We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.

Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices. Because each Business Resource Group is as unique as the population it serves, they offer a range of activities, networking opportunities, special events and learning programmes to associates.

Still founder-led by Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Richard Fairbank, Capital One is on a mission to help our customers succeed by bringing ingenuity, simplicity, and humanity to banking. We measure our efforts by the success our customers enjoy and the advocacy they exhibit. We are succeeding because they are succeeding.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment
jobs.description:
Our Company

The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission

The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

Your Impact

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, applies technical skill, experience, and subject-matter expertise in the areas of data management and analysis to support the ERO’s efforts to independently assess and report on the overall reliability, adequacy, and associated risks to the interconnected North American bulk power system. This Senior Data Analyst role includes responsibilities to collect, process, and analyze data necessary for assessing risks that could arise from the growing reliance on natural gas for electricity generation, with application to resource adequacy and bulk power system reliability assessments.

The Senior Data Analyst is part of the reliability assessment team that provides superior technical analysis and designs ERO processes for developing and publishing NERC’s reliability assessment reports, including the Long-Term Reliability Assessment and seasonal assessments. The Senior Data Analyst coordinates with the Performance Analysis team to provide reliability assessment information and analysis for the State of Reliability report and the Data and Analytics Integration team on data management, data quality, and analysis.

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, reports to the Manager, Reliability Assessments.

Your Role

Working with members of the reliability assessment team, analyze and interpret energy supply and infrastructure information, including: electricity generation, load, and transmission system data; and natural gas supply and infrastructure data.
Develop data requests and manage timely collection of reliability data from NERC registered entities to support the identification of electric reliability risks in NERC reliability assessments, with a focus on risks related to interdependent electric-natural gas energy systems.
Develop, implement and manage approaches, methods, and processes to promote data quality and reduce potential for data errors following best practices on data management.
Support the transformation of complex data into visualizations for use in NERC reliability assessments products.
Collaborate with NERC and ERO Enterprise subject matter experts that manage and use various reliability data systems on projects to make systems more compatible and interoperable.
Make use of available datasets containing generation, load, transmission, and natural gas fuel supply information to augment NERC’s collected data in analyzing trends and emerging risks to electric reliability.
Proactively identify and suggest solutions to technical analysis and data problems.
Develop working knowledge of the fundamentals of NERC Reliability Assessments.
Develop, implement and adhere to policies, procedures, and processes for the collection, storage, safeguarding, and authorized dissemination of data.
Support internal coordination with the Performance Analysis, Event Analysis, Engineering, Standards, and Compliance teams, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will have at a minimum:

BS in Engineering, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Management, or similar combination of education and training.
Previous experience within the energy sector performing a regulatory, monitoring, or analysis role.
Familiarity with publicly available historical energy data sets (EIA, DOE, FERC, Natural Gas Pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), etc.) as well as any pertinent proprietary data sets.
Intermediate-level computer and programming skills in applications such as Python, Microsoft SQL Server, and Excel (i.e., Macro, VBA, PowerPivot).
Exceptional interpersonal and communications skills, both oral and written.
Strong critical thinking and analytical skills and attention to detail.
Capability to work both independently and collaboratively on teams and support multiple tasks concurrently.

Preferred Candidates Will Also Have

Advanced degree and professional certifications or credentials.
Understanding of roles and responsibilities for North American bulk power system owners and operators.
Proficiency in writing for technical and general audiences.

Other

A background check will be conducted prior to employment.
In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.
This position has been classified as exempt.
The position may be based remotely but must be able to travel to NERC offices or meeting locations when needed. Reimbursement of travel expenses will be in accordance with the company’s travel and expense reimbursement policies.

Our Culture Declarations

Everyone at NERC is a leader.
We are accountable personally and organizationally to deliver on commitments.
We develop ourselves and people in the organization to ensure that NERC realizes its strategic objectives.
We are resilient and adaptable to the challenges and needs of the business and our team.
We exude a growth mindset and empower teams to take risks.
We build collaborative relationships within NERC, the ERO, and the stakeholders of NERC.
We exemplify NERC cultural behaviors:
Reward high-quality, creative, and innovative work
Attract, engage, and retain top talent
Value and respect diverse perspectives
Provide a safe, inclusive, and collaborative work environment
Form strong relationships within the company, and with the ERO Enterprise
We demonstrate curiosity in a wide variety of areas and are open to exploring new situations, knowledge, and opportunities for growth and development.
We demonstrate an anticipatory mindset, preventing problems and building contingencies where appropriate.
We are champions for diversity and inclusion, seeking out and values diverse perspectives.
We value well-being, prioritizing collaboration, engagement, and connection among our team.

jobs.description:
Are you a skilled Data Analyst passionate about making a difference in Australian rural healthcare?

The Australian College of Rural and Remote Medicine (ACRRM) is at the forefront of improving healthcare for rural, remote, and First Nations communities across Australia. We believe that robust data and insightful analysis are critical to understanding challenges, identifying opportunities, and ultimately delivering equitable and high-quality health services where they are needed most.
We are seeking a talented and committed Data Analyst to join our growing team. In this pivotal role, you will transform complex data into actionable insights that drive business decisions. As a Data Analyst, you will play a critical role in driving business performance by analysing large, complex datasets, identifying key trends, and providing actionable insights to stakeholders across the organisation. You will work with a variety of data sources, including trainee assessment and placement data, survey data, membership and transaction data, and leverage your analytical skills to solve challenging business problems. You will have a chance to contribute to high-impact projects, research, and play an important role in developing our data strategy. The position would suit someone with strong analytical capabilities and excellent communication skills to deliver meaningful insights to stakeholders across the organisation.

Your duties will include:

Data Analysis & Insight Generation: Analyse large-scale datasets from various sources using SQL and R (or similar programming languages) to identify trends, patterns, and opportunities that drive business growth and improve the experience of our members and stakeholders.
Reporting & Dashboard Development: Develop and maintain regular reporting systems and interactive dashboards using Power BI and Quarto/R Markdown to monitor business performance and key metrics.
Data Request Fulfilment: Respond to internal and external data requests, ensuring timely delivery of data insights across the College while maintaining regular reporting duties.
Collaboration & Solutions: Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to understand their diverse data needs and develop solutions that support their specific business objectives.
Visualisation & Communication: Create clear and compelling visualisations to communicate complex findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

To be successful in this role you must have:

Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.
Experience: 2+ years of experience in a data-driven role.
Proficiency in SQL for data extraction and manipulation.
Proficiency in R programming. Strong Python (or similar) programmers with a willingness to quickly learn R are also encouraged to apply.
Analytical Acumen: Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a strong attention to detail and a passion for uncovering insights from data.
Communication & Visualisation: Demonstrated ability to translate complex analyses into clear, actionable insights using effective visualisations in programs like Power BI.
Collaboration & Independence: Ability to work effectively in a team environment and collaborate with stakeholders across different departments, while also capable of working independently and managing multiple priorities.
Data Security Understanding: A solid understanding of data security principles, including access control, confidentiality, and anonymisation.
Eligibility to Work: Applicants must have the right to live and work in Australia.

About ACRRM

ACRRM is an accredited specialty medical college responsible for setting and maintaining professional standards for specialist general practitioners and rural generalists in Australia.
Nationally, ACRRM has more than 6,000 members, including Fellows, trainees and associate members, who live and work in rural, remote and First Nations communities across Australia. Members provide expert front line medical care in a diverse range of settings including general practices, hospitals, emergency departments, Aboriginal health services and other remote settings such as RFDS and the Australian Antarctic Division.
ACRRM’s core business is training and assessing specialist general practitioners for a rural generalist scope of practice, setting clinical standards for rural generalist practice; and support and advocacy services for rural, remote and First Nations communities and the health teams that serve them. Its vision is “Healthy rural, remote and First Nations communities through excellence, social accountability and innovation”.
The company’s headquarters is located in Brisbane, Queensland although the majority of staff work flexibly from state, regional or rural locations across the country. ACRRM offices are also located in Adelaide, Perth, Bunbury, Bendigo, Wodonga, Rockhampton, Darwin and Wollongong.
As part of living our values, we are visionary, courageous, experts and inclusive. We respect, inspire and support each other and believe in an inclusive workplace reflective of the communities in which we live and serve. The College recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce and is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. People living with a disability, those from culturally diverse backgrounds and First Nations people are encouraged to apply. Where appropriate, reasonable workplace accommodations will be provided to ensure equal opportunities for all.

Interested in joining our team?

For further information about the position, including the responsibilities or recruitment process, please contact James Dawber, Data Science and Analytics Manager, at j.dawber@acrrm.org.au

jobs.title: Platform Infrastructure Data Analyst
jobs.description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.

I&O Platform Infrastructure Data Analyst

The opportunity

In a plan to strengthen and extend our footprint in EY Enterprise Technology we are looking for a skilled Infrastructure Data Analyst to support and evolve EY's I&O data analytics and reporting capabilities globally. This is a unique role that bridges deep data analysis with practical infrastructure knowledge, enabling the firm to transform operational data from across its data center, compute, network, storage and observability platforms into actionable intelligence.

A key focus of this role is providing the analytical intelligence layer for the Hyperconverged Service Platform (HCSP) — EY's next-generation infrastructure automation platform built on Kubernetes, Temporal and Terraform. The Data Analyst will own the measurement, reporting and continuous improvement analysis of HCSP's provisioning performance, workflow reliability, SLA attainment, drift detection efficacy and operational impact across EY's global data center estate — directly enabling the platform team to measure success, identify failure patterns and demonstrate value.

Your Key Responsibilities

The I&O Platform Infrastructure Data Analyst collects, processes and analyzes operational data from across EY's infrastructure platforms — with a particular focus on HCSP platform telemetry — transforming raw data from workflow orchestration systems, provisioning engines, log aggregation platforms, ITSM tools and capacity management systems into meaningful insights and visualizations.

The role requires a strong analytical skill set combined with sufficient infrastructure and platform automation awareness to understand the context of the data being analyzed. The analyst will serve as the analytical authority for HCSP KPI reporting — tracking metrics such as provisioning SLA attainment, orchestrator failure rates, manual touchpoint reduction, rollback success rates and catalog drift elimination — and will partner with the HCSP engineering team, I&O leadership and service management to drive a data-informed culture of continuous platform improvement.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strong experience designing and delivering data analytics solutions using Power BI, including complex DAX measures, data models and report publishing.
Proficiency querying and analyzing data from ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana) including KQL query development and Kibana dashboard creation.
Experience working with large, multi-source operational datasets and transforming them into executive and operational reporting.
Ability to analyze and report on platform automation data, including:
Workflow execution metrics
OPA policy evaluation outcomes and policy compliance trends
Drift detection signals
ServiceNow order intake volumes, ticket correlation

Good understanding of data center infrastructure technologies including:
Windows Server and Linux operating system fundamentals
Virtualization platforms — Nutanix AHV, Hyper-V, VMware
Kubernetes cluster concepts — pods, namespaces, workloads and resource utilization
Network fundamentals — VLANs, DNS, IP management
Storage and compute provisioning concepts

Experience with SQL or KQL for querying structured and semi-structured data sources.
Experience integrating data from ITSM platforms (ServiceNow or equivalent) into analytical reporting.
Familiarity with APM and monitoring tooling (Dynatrace, SolarWinds, Prometheus or equivalent) as data sources.
Experience with ETL/ELT pipelines and data ingestion from multiple infrastructure and platform data sources.
Scripting capability to automate data extraction and transformation tasks:
Python (pandas, NumPy, requests)
PowerShell
Bash

Strong written and verbal communication skills — able to present HCSP performance findings and SLA trend analysis to both technical and senior business audiences.
Strong working knowledge of DevOps, Agile, Kanban, SCRUM and ITIL frameworks.
Ability to work effectively with global engineering and service management teams across multiple time zones.

To qualify for the role, you must have experience with

Power BI report and dashboard development — 5–7 years.
Power BI data modelling, DAX development and Power Query (M) transformations — 5–7 years.
ELK stack data analysis — Elasticsearch queries and Kibana dashboard development — 3–5 years.
SQL data analysis and querying against operational data stores — 5–7 years.
KPI definition, metric design and SLA/OLA reporting for platform or infrastructure services.
Data integration from ITSM platforms (ServiceNow, Remedy or equivalent).
Working with infrastructure and platform automation monitoring data — metrics, logs, workflow events and traces.
Building capacity planning and trend analysis reports for infrastructure and automation platforms.
Kubernetes and container platform telemetry consumption and analysis.
Workflow orchestration data analysis — Temporal, Argo or equivalent execution logs and metrics.
OPA policy evaluation data analysis and compliance reporting.
Drift detection and configuration audit data analysis.
Windows Server and Linux operating system concepts — sufficient to contextualize infrastructure data.
Virtualization platform familiarity (Nutanix AHV, Hyper-V, VMware vSphere or Azure Stack HCI).
Python scripting for data extraction, transformation and automation — 3–5 years.
PowerShell scripting for Windows infrastructure data collection.
Executive reporting and stakeholder presentation delivery.
Azure Monitor, Log Analytics or equivalent cloud observability data sources (preferred).
Working with CMDB data to enrich infrastructure and platform analytics (preferred).

Ideally, you'll also have

Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300) certification (desired).
Elastic Certified Analyst certification (desired).
Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals (DP-900) or Azure Data Engineer Associate (DP-203) (better to have).
ITIL v4 Foundation certification (exclusionary).
Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure Synapse Analytics or Databricks (better to have).
Experience with Grafana or similar open-source visualization platforms.
Familiarity with OpenTelemetry (OTel) as a telemetry standard for HCSP platform automation data.
Experience analyzing data from Temporal.io workflow execution APIs or audit logs.
Experience with Terraform state data and infrastructure drift analysis.
Experience operating within a managed services or large enterprise shared services environment.

What We Look For

A data-driven professional with a genuine curiosity for infrastructure platform operations and a talent for turning complex, multi-source operational data into clear and actionable insight. We are looking for an individual who combines strong analytical and visualization skills with practical infrastructure and platform automation awareness — enabling them to serve as the trusted analytical partner to EY's HCSP engineering team and I&O leadership, measuring the platform's impact, identifying improvement opportunities and demonstrating the value of automation at scale.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive remuneration package where you'll be rewarded for your individual and team performance. Our comprehensive Total Rewards package includes support for flexible working and career development. Plus, we offer:

Continuous learning: You'll develop the mindset and skills to navigate whatever comes next.
Success as defined by you: We'll provide the tools and flexibility, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.
Transformative leadership: We'll give you the insights, coaching and confidence to be the leader the world needs.
Diverse and inclusive culture: You'll be embraced for who you are and empowered to use your voice to help others find theirs.

EY | Building a better working world

EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.

Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.

Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

jobs.title: Wealth Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Advisors · RIAs · Portfolio Workflows

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

Our research connects more than 10,000 funds with institutional investors, 23,000+ advisory firms, and 400,000+ financial advisors, supporting fund discovery, portfolio analytics, and asset-manager distribution intelligence.

As a Wealth Research Analyst, you will study how financial advisors and wealth managers evaluate the funds PortfolioFuture identifies. The role covers advisor research, portfolio workflows, fund consideration, and the development of market intelligence used across PortfolioFuture.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.
• Study how advisors compare competing ETFs and mutual funds and what makes a fund worth further consideration.
• Document the recurring questions, objections, and concerns that come up around specific funds and investment strategies.
• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.
• Ability to understand an investment product well enough to discuss it with experienced advisors.
• Strong listening skills and the ability to identify patterns across many different conversations.
• Ability to turn qualitative feedback into clear, structured written findings.
• Comfort reaching out to and speaking with experienced wealth-management professionals.
• Ability to communicate what you learned clearly, including what you are not yet sure about.
• Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, investment product distribution, or practice management is useful but not required.
• Experience with research interviews, qualitative analysis, CRM data, or survey design is a plus.

PortfolioFuture research

Fund Substitution identifies ETFs and mutual funds that can serve similar portfolio roles, using return similarity, relative performance, tracking error, and fees.

Fund Decomposition separates returns explained by investable market exposures from residual performance, evaluating replication quality, residual alpha, and risk.

Fund Opportunity ranks ETFs and mutual funds across four dimensions: Similar Fund Ranking, Addressable Market, Pure Alpha, and Diversification Benefits.

PortfolioFuture’s research is independent. Commercial relationships do not affect which funds are surfaced, how they rank, or the conclusions reached.

Apply to PortfolioFuture positions on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/portfoliofuture

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Inference
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add.

We're Looking For a Technical Program Manager To Drive The Programs That Scale It. The Work Spans Four Closely Coupled Areas

Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online.
Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform.
Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request.
Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance.

This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like.

Key Responsibilities

Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery.
Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path.
Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision.
Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps.
Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org.
Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams.
Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion.
Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs.

Minimum Qualifications

7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it.
Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking.
A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly.
A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep.
The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers.
Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on.
Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit.
Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing.
Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform.
Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services.
Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity.
Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work.
Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling.
Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements.
Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$290,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:
Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

$290,000—$435,000 USD

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About The Team And Role

Welcome to our small but mighty TPM (Technical Program Management) team! We are the driving force that shapes how our company plans, prioritizes, and executes. As a Senior TPM, you will own program strategy and execution across our marketing organization, which owns two key pillars of work: Customer Operations and Brand Marketing.

Customer Operations is the pillar that reflects the voice of the customer back to the company, and the one that works to deliver an effortless customer support experience. You will partner with its leadership to drive the programs that connect that work to the rest of the company, from the voice of the customer program, to how that support experience is designed and delivered end to end, to the evolution of the operational model and team structure for Premium support.

Brand Marketing is the pillar that helps the company build and sustain brands people love and want to tell their friends about. You will act as the connector between brand strategy and product strategy and execution, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure the personality and identity of our brands are felt in the product itself and in our messaging and communications, which include larger brand campaigns as well as always-on communications.

You will drive the roadmap across both, connect them to the teams and leaders that depend on them, and bring a builder's instinct to the work, using AI and creative workflows to design better ways of running these programs.

About You

You are a thoughtful opinionator: you hold strong, well-reasoned views and are capable of voicing them respectfully to anyone, at any level. You are a proactive communicator who identifies possible problems before they surface.

You are a relationship builder and organizational navigator at heart, adept at building bridges across teams and functions. You are comfortable working with customer experience, marketing, and creative teams as well as product and engineering, able to follow the substance and hold your own with the subject matter experts you partner with.

You care about customers and about the power of building strong brands. You understand what a great customer experience is worth to a company, and you are intellectually curious about how brand personality and identity show up in consumer-facing products. You have been part of efforts that connected brand strategy to how a product is built and experienced.

You are already working with AI, and you have a point of view on where the TPM craft is headed in an increasingly agentic world. You have changed how you operate because of it.

You are a continuous learner with a growth mindset and an appetite for unfamiliar problems. Lastly, you are a voracious reader with a passion for books and the written and spoken word in all its forms!

What You Will Do

Act like an owner: Be an owner of program strategy and execution across our Customer Operations and Brand Marketing pillars, and serve as the connective tissue between those pillars and the partners they depend on.
Build relationships: Our TPM team thrives on collaboration. You will work closely with stakeholders at every level, from customer experience and marketing teams to engineers and executives, and your ability to build trust and align diverse perspectives will be central to what you can accomplish.
Drive strategy: You will dive deep into the how and the why of your programs, developing plans that connect day-to-day execution to where these pillars need to go. Your judgment will shape how decisions get made.
Decide what's worth doing: Partner with Customer Operations leadership to prioritize projects by customer impact, weigh them against team capacity, and defer or decline the rest. The customer's experience stays at the center of every tradeoff.
Connect marketing and product: Act as a connector between our marketing organization and our product-centric teams, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure brand is part of our key releases, in the product experience itself and in the messaging and communications around it.
Be a leader: Act as a leader within the TPM team. Identify opportunities to collaborate, share what works, and coach your teammates.
Lead beyond your pillars: Our TPM team also owns cross-company processes like yearly planning. You will contribute to these shared efforts and take a leadership role in shaping them.
Own the complexity: Drive multiple complex cross-functional programs simultaneously, and create scalable frameworks across pillars and functions to track work and communicate progress.
Enable your drivers: Many of the people driving and contributing to Customer Operations initiatives are also handling day to day frontline work and escalations. You will plan around their real capacity and give them structure and support, rather than assigning tasks and chasing updates.
Manage timelines: Lead the delivery timeline for your programs. Proactively identify risks and create mitigation strategies through workflows, communication, or resource allocation.
Measure success: Proactively propose success metrics for yourself and your programs, and identify when those metrics are at risk.
Build to move faster: Use AI and lightweight tooling to reduce the coordination tax on your teams. When you spot a manual, repetitive process, build something better.
Improve how we work: Identify and drive process improvements at the team and cross-team level, so the whole organization delivers at a larger scale.

We're looking for

5+ years of experience in a program management, operations, or equivalent role at a technology company.
A track record of operating independently, leading through ambiguity, and navigating complex organizational dynamics.
A structured approach to your work, paired with the judgment to know when to add process and when to remove it to reduce overhead and drive velocity.
Experience partnering closely with customer operations, marketing, or brand teams, and connecting their work to product and engineering teams.
An understanding of what great customer support is worth to a brand, and enough knowledge of brand to hold your own with marketers. You have worked with customer support teams, or know their workflows well enough to be a useful partner to them.
A customer-first lens in how you make decisions, with the judgment to weigh customer impact against efficiency.
Experience rolling out operational changes, such as process and tooling to a frontline team.
Strong familiarity with the software development process, working with product and engineering teams from roadmapping through delivery.
Experience working directly with product managers, engineers, marketers, and other subject matter experts.
Hands-on experience using AI in your work, and a clear point of view on how it changes the program management craft. You have already adjusted how you operate because of it.
Experience using data to identify problems and communicate solutions.
The ability to work and partner successfully across multiple functions in an organization.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to understand and articulate the big picture.
Distinctive problem-solving and analytical skills.

Bonus Points

You have held a program management role at a company where customer support sits at the heart of the brand.
You have seen up close how great customer support works, even if you have not worked in it directly.
You have run or helped run brand campaigns.
You have worked in a brand or marketing role earlier in your career.
You have designed AI workflows that enable customer operations or brand marketing teams to do their best work, whether that meant changing how a team handles its day-to-day or building something foundational they now can't imagine working without.

At Scribd, Inc., your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $124,000 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $172,000[maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $102,000 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $164,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $131,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $152,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

jobs.title: Lead Technical Program Manager, ADM (Remote)
jobs.description:
Job Title:

Lead Technical Program Manager, ADM (Remote)

Job Description:

The Role

Entegris is currently seeking a Lead, Technical Program Manager to join our Advanced Depositions Materials
team. This position can be based remotely in the US within a state that Entegris operates in.

The Technical Program Manager (TPM) is responsible for driving Advanced Deposition Materials (ADM) New Product Introductions (NPIs) from concept through release to high volume manufacturing. This role serves as the technical execution owner, ensuring alignment across Business Development, R&D, Engineering, Operations, and Manufacturing to deliver ADM products that meet customer requirements for performance, quality, and scalability.

This is a remote opportunity where the candidate can be based in the following states: MA, CT, PA, IL, TX, NV.

What You’ll Do

Drive New Product Introduction’ from concept/feasibility through release to High Volume Manufacturing (HVM) ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned to business priorities.
Define, track, manage, and report New Product Introduction PI milestones (sampling, development, HVM)
Identify and mitigate technical and executions risks across development and execution phases.
Coordinate cross functional execution to meet customer requirements, quality, and scale
Drive standardization of product development processes, tools, and best practices.
Identify process gaps and implement improvements to increase efficiency, quality, and scalability.
Promote data‑driven decision‑making and structured problem‑solving.
Aid in crafting customer communications to balance customer requirements, effective marketing of products, and strategic protection of information to maintain competitive advantage
Manage complex, high-impact programs that are critical to the business or customer

What We Seek

A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Engineering, Materials Science, or related degree/discipline is required
8+ years of direct experience with technical projects and strong understanding of engineering workflows, development of lifecycles, or manufacturing processes.
Preferred experience with advanced deposition technologies and/or new product development within semiconductor fabrication or related high-technology manufacturing environments.
Strong project management skills, including but not limited to, risk assessment and mitigation, conflict management, meeting management, task management, stakeholder management & project closure
Strong written & verbal communication skills
Strong stakeholder management skills and experience coordinating cross-functional teams.
Ability to translate technical ambiguity into clear execution plans.

Why Work at Entegris

Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future.

Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

What We Offer

Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

Compensation: The salary range for this position is $118,000-$180,000. Final compensation will be based on the candidate's overall skills and qualifications for the role.
Generous 401(K) plan with an impressive employer match
Excellent health, dental and vision insurance packages to fit your needs
Flexible work schedule and 11 paid holidays a year
Paid time off (PTO) policy that empowers you to take the time you need to recharge
Education assistance to support your learning journey
Values-driven culture with colleagues that rally around People, Accountability, Creativity and Excellence

Entegris does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need Entegris immigration sponsorship (e.g., H1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) now or in the future.

At Entegris we are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and applicants. Our policy is to recruit, hire, train, and reward employees for their individual abilities, achievements, and experience without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, marital or military status.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Project Manager, Wrike, Slack
jobs.description:
Higher education client is seeking a Project Manager to support their team. This is a 40 hour/week, fully remote opportunity beginning mid-November 2026 and extending through May 2026. While the role is fully remote, candidates located in the Los Angeles area are strongly preferred and may be asked to attend occasional walkthroughs and event-day activities.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
This Project Manager will lead the end-to-end management of print and digital marketing projects, supporting high-visibility admissions marketing efforts and large-scale university events.
IDEAL CANDIDATE:
The ideal candidate is an exceptionally organized marketing project manager who can successfully drive timelines, manage stakeholders, coordinate vendors and freelancers, and ensure high-quality execution across multiple workstreams. This role requires strong communication skills, meticulous attention to detail, and the ability to independently prioritize projects in a fast-paced environment.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
-Develop and maintain project schedules, calendars, and milestone tracking.
-Manage timelines and ensure all deliverables are completed on schedule.
-Track project budgets, costs, and spending throughout execution.
-Serve as the primary liaison between internal stakeholders, campus partners, vendors, freelancers, and creative teams.
-Lead project meetings by preparing agendas, facilitating discussions, capturing meeting notes, and following up on action items.
-Coordinate and manage print and digital marketing deliverables, including: event programs, signage, website content and digital assets, email marketing communications, social media content and event collateral and promotional materials.
-Manage content collection, organization, review cycles, and version control.
-Conduct quality assurance reviews to ensure accuracy, consistency, and brand standards are maintained across deliverables.
-Maintain organized project documentation, files, and archives.
-Draft, edit, and proofread communications and project materials for both internal and external audiences.
-Partner closely with the Senior Marketing Manager and provide support on special projects as needed.
REQUIRMENTS:
-Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field.
-2+ years of project management experience within marketing, advertising, creative services, communications, higher education, or a comparable environment.
-Familiarity with Wrike or other project management platforms, Microsoft Office, Zoom, Slack, and collaborative digital workspaces.
--Proven experience managing multiple projects simultaneously while balancing competing priorities and deadlines.
-Strong understanding of marketing and creative production workflows.
-Experience coordinating cross-functional teams, vendors, and stakeholders.
-Excellent organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
-Strong budgeting, cost tracking, and reporting experience.
-Strong proofreading, editing, and quality assurance capabilities.
-Experience taking detailed meeting notes and driving accountability for next steps.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
-Experience within higher education, university marketing, or admissions marketing environments.
-Familiarity with Wrike or other project management platforms.
-Experience working with Zoom, Slack, and collaborative digital workspaces.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About The Team And Role

Welcome to our small but mighty TPM (Technical Program Management) team! We are the driving force that shapes how our company plans, prioritizes, and executes. As a Senior TPM, you will own program strategy and execution across our marketing organization, which owns two key pillars of work: Customer Operations and Brand Marketing.

Customer Operations is the pillar that reflects the voice of the customer back to the company, and the one that works to deliver an effortless customer support experience. You will partner with its leadership to drive the programs that connect that work to the rest of the company, from the voice of the customer program, to how that support experience is designed and delivered end to end, to the evolution of the operational model and team structure for Premium support.

Brand Marketing is the pillar that helps the company build and sustain brands people love and want to tell their friends about. You will act as the connector between brand strategy and product strategy and execution, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure the personality and identity of our brands are felt in the product itself and in our messaging and communications, which include larger brand campaigns as well as always-on communications.

You will drive the roadmap across both, connect them to the teams and leaders that depend on them, and bring a builder's instinct to the work, using AI and creative workflows to design better ways of running these programs.

About You

You are a thoughtful opinionator: you hold strong, well-reasoned views and are capable of voicing them respectfully to anyone, at any level. You are a proactive communicator who identifies possible problems before they surface.

You are a relationship builder and organizational navigator at heart, adept at building bridges across teams and functions. You are comfortable working with customer experience, marketing, and creative teams as well as product and engineering, able to follow the substance and hold your own with the subject matter experts you partner with.

You care about customers and about the power of building strong brands. You understand what a great customer experience is worth to a company, and you are intellectually curious about how brand personality and identity show up in consumer-facing products. You have been part of efforts that connected brand strategy to how a product is built and experienced.

You are already working with AI, and you have a point of view on where the TPM craft is headed in an increasingly agentic world. You have changed how you operate because of it.

You are a continuous learner with a growth mindset and an appetite for unfamiliar problems. Lastly, you are a voracious reader with a passion for books and the written and spoken word in all its forms!

What You Will Do

Act like an owner: Be an owner of program strategy and execution across our Customer Operations and Brand Marketing pillars, and serve as the connective tissue between those pillars and the partners they depend on.
Build relationships: Our TPM team thrives on collaboration. You will work closely with stakeholders at every level, from customer experience and marketing teams to engineers and executives, and your ability to build trust and align diverse perspectives will be central to what you can accomplish.
Drive strategy: You will dive deep into the how and the why of your programs, developing plans that connect day-to-day execution to where these pillars need to go. Your judgment will shape how decisions get made.
Decide what's worth doing: Partner with Customer Operations leadership to prioritize projects by customer impact, weigh them against team capacity, and defer or decline the rest. The customer's experience stays at the center of every tradeoff.
Connect marketing and product: Act as a connector between our marketing organization and our product-centric teams, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure brand is part of our key releases, in the product experience itself and in the messaging and communications around it.
Be a leader: Act as a leader within the TPM team. Identify opportunities to collaborate, share what works, and coach your teammates.
Lead beyond your pillars: Our TPM team also owns cross-company processes like yearly planning. You will contribute to these shared efforts and take a leadership role in shaping them.
Own the complexity: Drive multiple complex cross-functional programs simultaneously, and create scalable frameworks across pillars and functions to track work and communicate progress.
Enable your drivers: Many of the people driving and contributing to Customer Operations initiatives are also handling day to day frontline work and escalations. You will plan around their real capacity and give them structure and support, rather than assigning tasks and chasing updates.
Manage timelines: Lead the delivery timeline for your programs. Proactively identify risks and create mitigation strategies through workflows, communication, or resource allocation.
Measure success: Proactively propose success metrics for yourself and your programs, and identify when those metrics are at risk.
Build to move faster: Use AI and lightweight tooling to reduce the coordination tax on your teams. When you spot a manual, repetitive process, build something better.
Improve how we work: Identify and drive process improvements at the team and cross-team level, so the whole organization delivers at a larger scale.

We're looking for

5+ years of experience in a program management, operations, or equivalent role at a technology company.
A track record of operating independently, leading through ambiguity, and navigating complex organizational dynamics.
A structured approach to your work, paired with the judgment to know when to add process and when to remove it to reduce overhead and drive velocity.
Experience partnering closely with customer operations, marketing, or brand teams, and connecting their work to product and engineering teams.
An understanding of what great customer support is worth to a brand, and enough knowledge of brand to hold your own with marketers. You have worked with customer support teams, or know their workflows well enough to be a useful partner to them.
A customer-first lens in how you make decisions, with the judgment to weigh customer impact against efficiency.
Experience rolling out operational changes, such as process and tooling to a frontline team.
Strong familiarity with the software development process, working with product and engineering teams from roadmapping through delivery.
Experience working directly with product managers, engineers, marketers, and other subject matter experts.
Hands-on experience using AI in your work, and a clear point of view on how it changes the program management craft. You have already adjusted how you operate because of it.
Experience using data to identify problems and communicate solutions.
The ability to work and partner successfully across multiple functions in an organization.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to understand and articulate the big picture.
Distinctive problem-solving and analytical skills.

Bonus Points

You have held a program management role at a company where customer support sits at the heart of the brand.
You have seen up close how great customer support works, even if you have not worked in it directly.
You have run or helped run brand campaigns.
You have worked in a brand or marketing role earlier in your career.
You have designed AI workflows that enable customer operations or brand marketing teams to do their best work, whether that meant changing how a team handles its day-to-day or building something foundational they now can't imagine working without.

jobs.title: Food Safety Program Manager II, WWGS Retail Food Safety
jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Oct 19, 2026

A typical day centers on keeping the Food Safety Audits programs running smoothly and the 3P auditor relationship healthy and productive. The Program Manager II leads the Worldwide Grocery Stores retail food safety audit program, partnering with a third party audit vendor, food safety analysts, store leadership, and cross functional stakeholders to ensure compliance with FDA Food Code.

Key job responsibilities

The role requires a results-oriented, analytical, customer-service approach to manage the audit program, measure progress, and drive risk management and compliance outcomes.

Manage the day-to-day execution of the Food Safety Audits programs, including the 3P Food Safety audit cycle — scheduling, coverage, standards alignment, and data integrity; works on one or more projects and may own a program.
Own accountability to the 3P Food Safety Auditor’s KPI scorecard; monitor audit completion, on-time delivery, scoring consistency, and finding-closure metrics, and act to keep them on target.
Manage the relationship with the 3P audit provider — align on audit standards and expectations, resolve data and scoring discrepancies, and hold the provider to KPI commitments.
Analyze and trend large audit data sets from internal and external audits to identify emerging Food Safety risks, recurring violations, and improvement opportunities.
Verify Food Safety policy and the FDA Food Code are correctly reflected in audit standards, checklists, and scoring criteria.
Support Food Safety escalations arising from audits; track corrective and preventive actions to closure with Operations stakeholders.
Optimize audit procedures, processes, and best practices to improve efficiency, data quality, and reporting cycle time.
Anticipate near-term bottlenecks in the audit program; identify, track, and mitigate immediate issues and risks, escalating when appropriate.
Write and publish audit performance and trend content for WWGS Business Reviews; convey findings and recommendations clearly to stakeholders.
Collaborate with AMZ & WFM stakeholders to align audit processes with Food Safety policy and Operations needs.
Stay informed of FDA Food Code updates, regulatory publications, and industry audit benchmarks, and apply them to the audit program.
Begin to mentor peers and new team members on audit standards, data analysis, and the FDA Food Code.
Make trade-offs across time, quality, and resources to deliver reliable audit outcomes; decide when to resolve independently versus escalate.

A day in the life

Day-to-day Responsibilities Include

Data governance of internal and third-party audits for stores across the US, Canada, and UK
Data analysis to identify process gaps and resolution
Maintaining relevant metrics for a food safety scorecard that measures each store's food safety performance
Reviewing and resolving clarifications
Monitor vendor performance through a KPI scorecard
Ownership of food safety self-audit questions and data
Creation and publishing of monthly and ad-hoc content for food safety culture (Food Safety Empowerment Teams)

About The Team

The Retail Food Safety team supports stores and company facilities with Food Safety policy, mechanisms to efficiently embed Food Safety in store processes, and a means to measure compliance. We bridge Food Safety to cross-functional stakeholders including Operations, Merchandising, Facilities, Procurement, and Leadership.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of program or project management experience
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
5+ years of managing food safety and quality in a large-scale retail or manufacturing environment experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Travel up to 25% of the time
CP-FS (Certified Professional – Food Safety) certification, or a comparable Food Safety professional certification.
Expertise in the FDA Food Code and retail food delivery/audit programs.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
3+ years of driving process improvements experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
Experience building processes, project management, and schedules
5+ years of working directly with government officials and regulatory bodies experience
